qt: to the Commission Alexander Jungbluth (ESN) Subject:

The European Social Fund co-financed the project ‘Bedarfsgemeinschaftscoaching MayenKoblenz’ (‘Coaching Communities of Need in Mayen-Koblenz) in 20211. According to the project description, the aim was to improve the employability of long-term benefit recipients, also by involving the entire ‘community of needs’, i.e. members of the household. This was to be achieved through outreach social work, systemic coaching, family dialogues and measures to stabilise the home environment. These are not conventional labour market-related measures such as upskilling or job placement, but socio-educational interventions whose impact on actual integration in the labour market is difficult to verify. 1.
Exactly how much EU funding did the project ‘Bedarfsgemeinschaftscoaching MayenKoblenz 2021’ receive, and what measurable placement outcomes did it report to the Commission?
How does the Commission justify providing funding from the European Social Fund for primarily socio-educational projects, the direct effects on the labour market of which it considers to be modest?

Does the Commission consider there to be an overstepping of European competences in the use of EU funds for locally defined coaching formats by municipal social authorities without clear structural policy added value?
